title: Add contrastive-pair odds-ratio gate and randomized-suffix prober CI hook
author: Priya Nambiar
description:
Motivation: We frequently see subtle regressions where a model's relative ranking between semantically equivalent positive/negative contrastive pairs drifts (e.g., preferred vs. not-preferred completions) even when absolute metrics look stable. This PR introduces an automated CI hook that computes an odds-ratio style stability metric on contrastive prompt pairs and a complementary randomized-suffix prober to detect suffix sensitivity regressions.

What this PR adds: a) contrastive_odds_gate: a CI hook that runs a batch of labeled contrastive pairs (A/B style) and computes an aggregated odds ratio and confidence interval using bootstrap resampling; the gate fails if the odds ratio drops below a configurable threshold or if the lower bootstrap CI crosses 1.0. b) randomized_suffix_prober: a small probe harness that appends randomized suffix tokens (common punctuation, short phrases, user-like trailing tokens) to prompts to measure sensitivity; outputs a stability score per prompt-set. c) an eval-gate config so teams can opt-in specific prompt sets and thresholds for their repo/route. d) smoke tests and integration test vectors to validate the hook behavior in CI.

Implementation notes: The odds ratio gate treats each contrastive example as a binary win/loss (model selects preferred completion). The gate aggregates across the prompt set to compute odds = (wins + 0.5) / (losses + 0.5) with small-sample smoothing and performs 1k stratified bootstrap resamples to estimate a 95% CI. Randomized suffix probing generates 10 perturbations per prompt by sampling from a curated suffix pool (commonly observed trailing tokens in production traces) and measures maximum relative rank shift across perturbations. Both components are implemented as lightweight Python modules that call the existing eval harness runner API; they do not change model-serving code.

Config and rollout: New CI config file ci/configs/eval_gate.yaml demonstrates two gate profiles: conservative (odds_ratio_threshold=0.9, min_examples=200) and permissive (0.7, min_examples=50). Default behavior is opt-in; the gate is included in the eval-harness CI matrix but disabled for repos that don't list the profile. We will ship with the 'core-stability' prompt set and start enforcement on smaller teams as a beta to gather false-positive rates.

Backwards compatibility: Existing eval hooks are untouched. The new gate uses the standard hook interface so it can be added to existing pipelines without code changes to runners.

Performance: Typical run time for the core-stability set (~400 pairs) is ~40-60s using batched calls against the local mock runtime; added cost in hosted CI is modest because we reuse cached model artifacts and use small batch sizes.

Why this is different: Instead of only tracking absolute metric deltas, the odds-ratio gate explicitly captures relative preference shifts between paired examples and complements per-prompt suffix robustness checks. This helps catch regressions where overall BLEU/EM remains stable while model behavior flips on important decision points.

Add randomized suffix prober to detect sensitivity to trailing tokens
Configurable gate profiles and example prompt sets included
Docs and examples for onboarding teams to the gate
